elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service and that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. Section 12.4 affirmatively permits Customer to develop, market, sell, or acquire competing products or services.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction on Customer is limited to a specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: the rendered language imposes no non-compete restriction on Customer, so there is no broader unnamed-product restriction.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction applies only during the term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: no non-compete restriction applies during or after the term. The reference in Section 12.4 to the term and the following twenty-four months qualifies an affirmative permission, not a restriction.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction is capped at twelve months.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: no non-compete restriction exists, and therefore none exceeds twelve months.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction includes a carve-out for Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent; moreover, Sections 12.3 and 12.4 affirmatively preserve Customer's ability to develop products and services.

elements.element: Any non-compete restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions by Customer.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent; moreover, Sections 12.3 and 12.4 affirmatively preserve Customer's ability to acquire products and services.

result.reason: The operative language fully achieves the preferred position by replacing the prohibition in Section 12.4 with affirmative permission and retaining Section 12.3's broad disclaimer of restrictions. The fallback limitations are also satisfied because they are maximum constraints on any non-compete, and no non-compete exists. The change is substantively minimal and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms. Drafting quality is reduced because Section 12.4 unnecessarily retains the twenty-four-month period in an affirmative permission, creating redundancy and a possible negative implication after that period, although Section 12.3 resolves that implication.
